Class KineticsModel

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.mdi3D.view3D.kineticsDemo.KineticsModel
public class KineticsModel extends Object
A physics model simulating particles in a 3D box with elastic collisions.

The model maintains an internal mutable state (positions + velocities) and exposes an optimized, UI-friendly SimulationSnapshot containing only a reference to a packed float[] coordinate buffer.

Double buffering (front/back)

  • The simulation thread writes new positions into the back buffer.
  • After the update, buffers are swapped so the front buffer is always the most recently completed frame.
  • getSnapshot() is side-effect free and simply returns the current front buffer.

    • reset

      public void reset(int count, float length, float volumeFraction, float initialTemp)
      Reinitialize the simulation with a new particle count and starting conditions, discarding any in-progress state.

      Particles are placed at random positions within a cubic sub-region of side length * volumeFraction (so the gas starts confined to one corner of the box) and given Maxwell–Boltzmann-distributed velocities corresponding to initialTemp.

      Unlike the constructor, count and length here need not match the values originally passed to the constructor: the coordinate buffers are reallocated to the new count, and the new length becomes the elastic-wall bounding box used by update() and the occupancy histogram used by computeEntropy(), exactly as if a new KineticsModel had been constructed.

      Must not be called concurrently with update() from another thread; neither method synchronizes against the other.

      Parameters:
      count - number of particles to create
      length - new side length of the bounding cube, used both for the initial confined sub-region and as the elastic-wall box for subsequent updates
      volumeFraction - fraction of length defining the initial confined sub-region, in (0, 1]
      initialTemp - initial temperature, used to set the standard deviation of the initial velocity distribution
